intro: Loss prevention specialists watch for theft, judge situations quickly and work with police and store staff. The closest of the 25 careers below is supervising security workers, with an 89% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $55,940, and most options need no more education.
why_it_works: The job means watching cameras and the sales floor, investigating losses and handling confrontations calmly and legally. O*NET rates judgment and social perceptiveness at 3.38 out of 5 for this job and coordination at 3.12. Security, detective and corrections work use the same skills. BLS reports this job within a broader group, so this page shows medians instead of percent changes.
tips: Security supervision is the closest move and builds the leadership experience managers need.
Detectives and Criminal Investigators earn $93,790 and are a 79% match, after academy training.
Loss Prevention Managers earn $141,900 for their broader group, usually with a bachelor's degree.

faq.q: What jobs can former loss prevention specialists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are security worker supervisors (89%), detectives and criminal investigators (79%) and Loss Prevention Managers (79%), based on O*NET 31.0. Correctional officers are 77% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $58,940 with on-the-job academy training.

faq.q: Which jobs for loss prevention specialists pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 25 matches, the highest medians are Loss Prevention Managers at $141,900, Compliance Managers at $141,900 and Security Managers at $106,660, according to BLS May 2025 data. All three are reported within broader BLS groups and usually need a bachelor's degree.

faq.q: Do loss prevention specialists need a degree to switch?
faq.a: For some paths. 20 of the 25 matches need no more education than loss prevention specialists already have, including 7 of the top 10. An associate degree is common in the closest match, held by 30% of workers, though experience in retail security counts heavily.

faq.q: What skills should loss prevention specialists learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are persuasion, instructing, managing people and complex problem solving. Systems analysis already rates 3 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so leading and training teams is the main step toward management roles.
